revisedDesign.summary: BUG-3: classify once at the provider boundary from vendor-typed fields. Carry the StopCategory through the loop error arms (required there) and the kernel terminal. At goal settlement, project it onto the EXISTING Blocker/BlockerObservation model instead of a new receipt field. Stop-class failures add a dependency-keyed blocker in the same settleAttempt commit, so the goal derives `blocked` and the wake skips 'not-active'. Retry-class failures record a host observation that promotes to a blocker under the existing 3-distinct-attempt rule. Fix the web stall with one SESSION_STATUS_SETTLED table, and gate the usage_limited producer by kind. BUG-4: web and CLI attach submit one turn.run{input} command, negotiated by capability. The kernel records once what the running turn started with, so approval resume never keys on draftInput. On the web, one command-outcome SSOT models settled / rejected / admitted-earlier / undelivered / outcome-unknown, with no timer; resending the same commandId is idempotent. On delivery the composer text moves into a pending-submission entry and is restored on rejection, so queueing still works.
revisedDesign.structuralMechanism: (1) SSOT of failure meaning: an `LLM_ERROR_KINDS` const tuple in src/shared/errors.ts, with `type LLMErrorKind = (typeof LLM_ERROR_KINDS)[number]`. Drift is impossible, and the two hand-typed test copies are deleted. One `classifyProviderError(provider, e)` with a fixed precedence: abort → no status: transport code (e.code or e.cause.code ∈ NETWORK_CODES ∪ measured Bun 'ConnectionRefused') → network, otherwise unknown → vendor-typed code/type row (exact equality) → STATUS_KIND (+402→quota_exhausted) → 400/422 classifyBadRequest (marker lists live ONLY here) → 5xx. One structured extractor, `providerErrorFields: Record<LLMProvider, (e) => {type?, code?}>`, replaces extractProviderCode and lowerProviderCode. Vendor rows: ANTHROPIC_ERROR_TYPE_KIND: Record<AnthropicErrorType, LLMErrorKind | 'by-status'> over a src tuple, with a type-only two-way check against @anthropic-ai/sdk ErrorObject['type'] in src/llm; OPENAI_ERROR_CODE_KIND (partial, exact codes; unknown → by-status); RESPONSE_ERROR_CODE_KIND: Record<ResponseError['code'], LLMErrorKind> for response.failed. The fetch path goes through LLMError.fromHttpResponse, which runs the same extractor over the parsed body and headers. (2) A string-only loop failure is unrepresentable: RecoveryAction {do:'error'} and TurnResult {kind:'error'} REQUIRE `stopCategory: StopCategory`. It is produced only by stopCategoryForFailure(error) = STOP_REASON_CODE_BY_LLM_ERROR_KIND[kind] (Record<LLMErrorKind, StopReasonCode>), runtime.unknown_error for non-LLMError values, and named constructors for loop terminals. classifyErrorReason is deleted. The SessionHost port (AgentOutcome.stopCategory) stays optional because it is an external port; a missing category projects to stopCategoryForReason. (3) The goal projection reuses the blocker model. GOAL_FAILURE_DISPOSITION: Record<StopReasonCode, {kind:'none'} | {kind:'observe'} | {kind:'block', waitingOn}>, with a runtime guard over Object.values(STOP_REASON_CODE). The host passes `failure {disposition, dependencyId:'turn-failure:<code>' | 'turn-failure:transient', reason: STOP_PRESENTATION label, waitingOn}` inside ObjectiveAttemptSettlement. The authority applies it in the SAME settleAttempt commit (one revision bump): block → core.addDependencyBlocker, which dedupes by dependencyId and reuses promoteObservedBlocker; observe → core.observeBlocker with attemptId, skipped when gainedProgress. No receipt field and no schema migration. Only a user or system clearBlocker lifts it; model and continuation actors cannot (policy.ts:97). (4) SESSION_STATUS_SETTLED: Record<KernelSessionState['status'], boolean>, over a KERNEL_SESSION_STATUSES tuple, is the single answer to 'may new work start'. It is read by goal-wake-compose, goal-work-compose and the turn.submit reducer guard. (5) USAGE_WINDOW_BY_KIND: Record<LLMErrorKind, boolean> (only rate_limit true) gates markObjectiveUsageLimitedFrom429. (6) BUG-4 kernel SSOT: KernelSessionState.activeTurnInput {prompt, images, provenance?} is written ONLY by startTurn (kernel-internal, never projected) and cleared by terminals. pausedTurnOf returns it and the command-type ternary is deleted, so a new start path cannot lose the prompt. (7) Wire: TurnRunCommand.input?, codec validation, and a reducer arm that refuses when a draft is non-empty. The `inlineTurnInput` capability marker ensures new clients never send input to an old daemon. (8) Web: dispatchCommand(client, command, settledWhen) → Promise<CommandOutcome>, a closed union {settled|rejected{reason,issue}|admitted-earlier|undelivered|outcome-unknown}. The raw socket send is renamed to the unique token `sendRaw`, used only by that module. The composer clear lives only inside submitTurn.

revisedDesign.compatibilityAndMigration: Persistence: no schema change. Blockers and observations with dependencyId are already in the v2 schema (saved-session-schema.ts:251-252) and restore (restore.ts:285-306). An older binary reading a new file sees an ordinary blocked goal with a label as its reason, and its existing /goal unblock clears it. Receipts are unchanged. Wire: TurnFailedEvent.stopCategory, TurnRunCommand.input and capabilities.inlineTurnInput are all additive. An old frontend against a new daemon still uses the accepted legacy append+run path. A new frontend against an old daemon sees no marker (normalized false) and uses the legacy pair keyed on the run commandId, with draft restore on rejection. A client that ignores the marker and sends input to an old daemon hits the codec pass-through hazard described in WC6. LLMErrorKind gains quota_exhausted; the exhaustive switches (codex-spec-router, default-classifier) fail to compile until handled, so typecheck:all is mandatory because bun test does not typecheck. StopReasonCode gains 5 codes, none renamed; the web mirror and drift hellgate update in the same commit. Behavior changes: a 429 that mentions 'too many tokens' no longer compacts; an empty or truncated stream is labeled network instead of rate_limit (retry unchanged); an overload or 503 with retry-after no longer marks usage_limited; auth, quota/billing, model-unavailable, policy, bad-request, context and compaction-thrash failures block the goal until /goal unblock; three distinct transient-failure attempts without progress block it; kernel 'failed' counts as settled for web wake, /goal work and turn.submit. Anthropic mid-stream SSE errors stay kind unknown and are retried through the existing marker fallback unless decision D7 is taken.
revisedDesign.userVisibleBehavior: CLI: a revoked key or exhausted quota ends the turn with the raw error plus (decision D9) `stopped: Provider auth failed — <hint>`. /goal shows `status: blocked`, `blockers (/goal unblock to clear): - [user] Provider auth failed`, and `wake: idle (not-active)`. No further autonomous provider call happens until the user runs /goal unblock. Transient failures (overload, network, 5xx, unknown, or empty/truncated model output) keep today's backoff and show `(observing N/3)`; after three distinct failed attempts without progress the goal is blocked with 'turn-failure:transient'. Physical calls per quota failure drop from 60 to 3 on the chat-SDK path, or to 1 with decision D5. A 429 with retry-after on the default surface shows usage-limited with the exact retry time, and an overload no longer claims 'usage limit'. Web: failed turns show a typed badge and hint, and a failed goal turn no longer freezes pursuit as not-quiescent. A sent message appears as a queued entry even while another turn runs. If the daemon rejects it, the text returns to the composer with the reason. If the socket drops before confirmation, the entry says it is not confirmed and offers Resend, which cannot create a duplicate turn. Messages from separate sends are never glued together.
revisedDesign.rollout: Default-on, with no feature gate. These are honesty and correctness fixes to default-on paths: goal pursuit and objectiveBudgetEnforce are default-ON (runtime-config.ts:225-262), and the web composer is always on. Gating the fixes would leave the 60-call burn, the web stall and the lost-draft bug live by default, while code behind a default-OFF gate goes unexercised. inlineTurnInput is compatibility negotiation, not a flag. QUANTA_GOAL=0 remains the opt-out for goal pursuit itself. The retry-owner consolidation (D5) and treating a truncated stream as an error (D6) ship only on user decision.

userDecisions.question: D1: What should an unrecoverable provider or turn failure (auth, quota/billing, model unavailable, policy, bad request, context limit, compaction thrash) do to an active goal?
userDecisions.options: (a) Add a dependency-keyed system blocker in the settlement commit. The goal becomes 'blocked' and the wake skips it. Only the user's /goal unblock lifts it. It survives attach and restart with no schema change (probe pl). (b) Clear the goal the way Claude Code does ('Goal cleared after an unrecoverable error… Run /goal again', chunk-3j0en1hg.js:158913-158934). This discards the criteria and verifier evidence. (c) R1's receipt field plus revision fence. Attach and continuation bypass it (probe pa).

userDecisions.question: D2: What should repeated transient failures (overload, network, 5xx, unknown, or malformed/empty/truncated model output) do?
userDecisions.options: (a) Record a host observation under dependencyId 'turn-failure:transient' and reuse the existing rule that promotes to a blocker after 3 distinct attempts (criteria-ops.ts:61-63). Progress clears it. (b) No cap: keep today's no-progress backoff up to the product cap of 20 autonomous turns. (c) Claude Code's reprompt schedule [60s, 300s, 900s], then pause. This adds new constants.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). It adds no new number, and both the Claude Code and Codex baselines stop at about 3.

userDecisions.question: D3: Confirm the default disposition for each stop code.
userDecisions.options: Defaults. Block: provider.auth, provider.quota_exhausted, provider.model_unavailable, provider.policy, provider.bad_request, provider.context_window, compaction.thrash. Observe: provider.rate_limit, provider.overloaded, provider.network, provider.server_error, provider.unknown, runtime.unknown_error, model.malformed_tool_use, model.empty_exhausted, model.output_truncated. None: completed.*, user.interrupt, system.abort, shell.needs_approval, turn.awaiting_approval, budget.*, model.refusal, loop.no_progress. Alternatives to consider: provider.bad_request → observe; system.abort (content filter) → block.
userDecisions.recommendation: Accept the defaults. They follow Claude Code's stop/pause/retry split (chunk-3j0en1hg.js:159031-159130), with pause folded into block because both need the user to act.

userDecisions.question: D4: Should OpenAI insufficient_quota and Anthropic billing_error/402 be one error kind or two?
userDecisions.options: (a) One kind, quota_exhausted, labeled 'Provider quota or billing limit reached'. providerCode keeps the vendor detail. (b) Separate kinds and stop codes for quota_exhausted and billing.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). The user's fix and the routing are the same for both, and one kind keeps the change smallest.

userDecisions.question: D5: Which layer should own retries? Measured: 60 physical provider calls in one turn for a 529 or a chat-SDK insufficient_quota under the production RetryingLLM wrap (probe pm).
userDecisions.options: (a) Set the vendor SDK's maxRetries to 0 so quanta's typed router owns retries (RetryingLLM before the stream, loop recovery after). That gives 20 calls for a 529 and 1 for a quota error. (b) Also stop loop recovery from retrying kinds that RetryingLLM already retried, for about 5 calls. (c) Keep today's behavior.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a) now, as a separate commit; (b) as a follow-up after measuring. The SDK cannot see quanta's typed error kinds.

userDecisions.question: D6: A Responses stream that ends after content but without response.completed currently completes silently. Should it be an error?
userDecisions.options: (a) Throw kind network, matching Codex ('stream closed before response.completed'); the partial turn is retried. (b) Keep completing silently. The new `error` SSE handler already covers errors the provider announces.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a), once you have checked that no OpenAI-compatible proxy in use omits response.completed.

userDecisions.question: D7: For a mid-stream Anthropic SSE error, should quanta parse the ErrorResponse JSON the SDK puts in APIConnectionError.message?
userDecisions.options: (a) Strictly schema-parse it at the adapter boundary, labeled as a parse of the message field (streaming.js:53-54). (b) Leave it as kind unknown. It is retried through the RETRYABLE_MARKERS fallback and labeled 'Provider error'.
userDecisions.recommendation: (b) for now. It does not change goal behavior (it is observe-class), and the SDK exposes no structured field for it.

userDecisions.question: D8: Anthropic's 400 'credit balance is too low' has no structured billing type (its type is invalid_request_error). Should quanta add a text marker at the boundary to catch it?
userDecisions.options: (a) No marker: it stays kind bad_request, which blocks the goal with 'Provider rejected the request'. (b) Add one documented boundary marker that maps it to quota_exhausted, as Claude Code does (chunk-3j0en1hg.js:102244).
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). The goal is blocked either way; only the label differs.

userDecisions.question: D9: Should the CLI print a typed stop line for errored turns and show a blocker label on the goal checkpoint line?
userDecisions.options: (a) Yes: print `stopped: <label> — <hint>` and append `· blocked: <label>`. (b) Keep only the raw `error:` text.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). It serves the north star of showing why the agent stopped and what to do next.

userDecisions.question: D10: How should a web message submit be made atomic?
userDecisions.options: (a) Add an input field to turn.run, advertised by an inlineTurnInput capability marker, with the kernel recording the running turn's input in one place (activeTurnInput). (b) Add a new `turn.send` command type. The kernel checks `command.type === 'turn.run'` literally in several places (scheduler.ts:112, 325, 348), which would silently skip cancel registration and the pre-abort gate for the new type. (c) Client-only: two receipts over the existing append+run. A stranded draft is still possible.

userDecisions.question: D11: How should the composer behave while a submission is unconfirmed?
userDecisions.options: (a) On delivery, clear the composer and show a visible pending-submission entry. Restore the text on rejection, and offer Resend (same commandId) when the outcome is unknown. Queueing a message behind a running turn keeps working. (b) Keep the text in the composer and disable send until turn.started. That blocks queueing for the whole previous turn (probe pf). (c) Codex desktop style: refuse any new submission while one is unconfirmed (app-initial…js:131839).

userDecisions.question: D12: How should an unknown outcome be resolved after reconnecting?
userDecisions.options: (a) A manual Resend action that sends the identical frame again. It is idempotent while the daemon stays up, within the bridge's 128-command dedup window (probe pn). (b) Resend automatically on reconnect.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a). After a daemon restart the dedup window is gone, so an automatic resend could duplicate a turn that already ran.

userDecisions.question: D13: A legacy client left a draft stranded in the kernel, so the inline submit is refused with turn_run_draft_not_empty. How should the user recover?
userDecisions.options: (a) Show the server's draftInput alongside the rejection and offer 'Send pending draft', which sends a bare turn.run (no new command). (b) Add a new input.clear command. (c) Concatenate the draft with the new text (today's behavior; rejected).

userDecisions.question: D14: Should the web frontend get a DOM environment (jsdom) so tests can mount App and the composer?
userDecisions.options: (a) Install jsdom as a devDependency and set the vitest environment. Installs are blocked on this box per memory. (b) Test the extracted controller over FakeWebSocket, plus a static pin, labeled as such, that App is wired to it. No install needed.

userDecisions.question: D15: Should real provider error responses be recorded as test fixtures?
userDecisions.options: (a) Capture a real 401 from each vendor using a deliberately invalid key (free). If a real exhausted account exists, also capture quota and billing errors. Store them with provenance. (b) Keep only bodies built from the SDK types, labeled as such.
userDecisions.recommendation: (a) for the 401s. Quota and billing bodies stay SDK-typed and marked UNVERIFIED until captured.

userDecisions.question: D16: Should the public SDK session verbs (input.append/turn.run in handle-verbs.ts, and sdk/runtime/session.ts) get an atomic send verb?
userDecisions.options: (a) Add turn.run({input}) to the verb surface now. (b) Do it as a follow-up. The in-process runtime verbs cannot lose a frame; the remote handle can.
userDecisions.recommendation: (b), tracked as a follow-up for the remote handle.

residualRisks: Vendor SDK unions can drift from the live API. SDK 0.40.1's ErrorObject lacks request_too_large (413), which the API doc lists. Types outside the union fall back to status. An exhaustive Record proves the SDK union is covered, not the API.

OpenAI error codes (insufficient_quota, invalid_api_key, model_not_found) and the ChatGPT usage_limit_reached/resets_at body come from public docs and Codex symbol tokens, not live captures (UNVERIFIED). Whether insufficient_quota appears on the Responses SSE error event is also UNVERIFIED.

Bun fetch/connection error codes other than the measured 'ConnectionRefused' (resets, DNS, TLS) stay kind unknown until measured. They are retried only through the surviving RETRYABLE_MARKERS fallback for kind unknown (retry.ts:161-164), a downstream text path this plan does not remove.
Bedrock and Vertex error bodies (x-amzn-errortype, google.rpc) are not captured, so those transports stay status-only.

The web command dedup window holds 128 commands with FIFO eviction. A pending entry can be evicted by 128 newer commands, and after a daemon restart a same-id resend can re-run a turn that already ran. D12 keeps resend manual for this reason.

An in-process pre-aborted turn.run with inline input settles without turn.started (scheduler-turn-execution.ts:280-300), so the client outcome stays unsettled until the connection changes. This is rare on the wire path (UNVERIFIED).
A turn-failure blocker persists its reason label as text. If a presentation label is later renamed, old blockers keep the old label; dependencyId still carries the code.

Treating kernel 'failed' as settled widens turn.submit admission. The serial dispatch queue (engine.ts:104-110) should prevent a race with a host that is still settling, but only F-T4/F-T5 show this; no adversarial round has checked it yet.
bun test does not typecheck. The required-category and kind-widening ripple is caught only by typecheck:all, and the compile pins run only there.

The web vitest suite runs in the node environment and cannot mount App, so App wiring is guarded only by a labeled static pin (D14). GH Actions may still be billing-blocked (memory aug-22, not re-checked), which would leave the prepush web-frontend gate as the effective check.
The subagent failure path (a role-model-override provider failing inside a child agent) is untraced and would not reach goal settlement (MH10).

Concurrent sessions commit to main; the working tree already shows modifications from another session. Re-check HEAD before each commit and never rewrite refs. The plan adds no _arch scan-guard enrollment, to avoid colliding with the sep-12 campaign.
